overview: FactSet is a global provider of integrated financial data, analytics, and workflow software for the investment community, delivering content through its flagship Workstation, data feeds, portfolio analytics, and enterprise solutions. Founded in 1978 and headquartered in Norwalk, Connecticut, the subscription-based business serves roughly 9,100+ client firms and 237,000+ individual professional users spanning institutional asset managers, hedge funds, wealth managers, banks, corporates, and private equity/venture capital, with buy-side clients (~82% of ASV) far outweighing sell-side (~18%). Revenue is roughly 65% Americas, 25% EMEA, and 10% Asia Pacific, and the company operates on an August 31 fiscal year-end.

business_model.summary: FactSet sells forward-looking, recurring subscriptions measured internally as Annual Subscription Value (ASV) — the next-12-months run-rate of all subscription services currently supplied to clients — rather than reporting product-line revenue splits publicly. Growth is driven by a mix of price increases, upsells to existing clients (the primary driver), new client wins, and, to a lesser extent, acquisitions (e.g., LiquidityBook, Irwin) net of any divestitures/attrition. Gross client retention runs above 95% and organic ASV growth has been running 5.5-7.1% year-over-year through FY2025-FY2026, an acceleration management attributes partly to AI-related product adoption. Average client tenure exceeds 16 years, with nine of the top 10 clients (by ASV) having been with FactSet for more than two decades, reflecting extremely high revenue durability once a client is onboarded.

revenue_streams.name: Workstation/Research (desktop analytics, data, and workflow platform)
Analytics & Trading / Content & Technology Solutions (CTS) — enterprise data feeds, managed services
Other (Irwin IR/capital markets platform, LiquidityBook OMS/trading, Real Estate solutions)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/enterprise subscriptions — institutional asset managers, hedge funds, wealth managers, banks/sell-side, asset owners, corporates, and private equity/VC firms; contracts increasingly structured as multi-year enterprise agreements (average renewed contract term extended ~30% in recent quarters) rather than single-seat licenses
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas ~65%, EMEA ~25%, Asia Pacific ~10% of total revenue (FY2025)

main_competitors: Numerous fintech/AI-native data and analytics startups
competitive_position.market_position: A top-tier but not dominant player in the financial data/analytics terminal market; industry estimates put Bloomberg at roughly one-third market share, Refinitiv/LSEG around 20%, S&P Capital IQ around 6%, and FactSet around 4-5%, with FactSet punching above that share in portfolio analytics, buy-side workflow, and increasingly wealth management and IR/capital markets (via Irwin) and trading/OMS (via LiquidityBook).

moat_factors.description: Client relationships average 16+ years with 95%+ ASV retention; workflows, custom analytics, and integrations become deeply embedded in client operations, making rip-and-replace costly and risky for institutional users.

Proprietary aggregation and normalization of fundamental, estimates, ownership, fixed income, and alternative datasets across thousands of sources, combined with portfolio analytics tools, creates a defensible integrated offering that is hard to replicate piecemeal.

CTS/data feed and API business embeds FactSet data directly into client-built systems and now into third-party AI platforms (Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude via Cowork), extending the moat beyond the desktop Workstation and creating a defensible role as a trusted, auditable data layer for AI agents in regulated finance.

moat_factors.factor: Brand and reputation for data quality/compliance
moat_factors.description: Decades-long reputation for accuracy and audit trails in a highly regulated industry, valuable as AI agent outputs increasingly require sourced, defensible data — a differentiator FactSet is actively marketing against generic LLM tools.

Large fixed cost base in data licensing, content operations (including offshore data operations in India), and R&D is spread across a large global client base, though this scale advantage is smaller than Bloomberg's or LSEG's.

weaknesses: Smaller scale than Bloomberg and LSEG/Refinitiv, limiting negotiating leverage with data suppliers and constraining pricing power in head-to-head competitive takeaways
Sell-side ASV (~18% of book) is more cyclical and tied to investment banking headcount/budgets, which have been volatile

Perceived vulnerability to AI/LLM-based tools that could commoditize basic data retrieval and analysis, compressing the value of legacy workstation seats — the dominant bear narrative that cut the stock roughly in half from its 2025 highs
Historically modest revenue growth (mid-single-digit ASV growth) relative to software peers, making the stock reliant on margin expansion and buybacks for EPS growth
Integration risk from a more acquisitive posture (LiquidityBook, Irwin) after years as a largely organic grower

growth_drivers: AI product adoption inside the FactSet platform: management reports clients using FactSet AI solutions are growing ASV roughly 50% faster than the rest of the client base, and over 90% of the top 50 clients now use four or more FactSet AI solutions

Strategic partnership with Google Cloud (announced June 2026) embedding Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform capabilities into the Workstation and building jointly developed agents for portfolio operations, deal advisory, and corporate finance

Distribution of FactSet data into third-party AI ecosystems, including a connector enabling FactSet market data inside Anthropic's Claude (via Cowork, February 2026), positioning FactSet as a trusted, auditable data layer for AI agents rather than being purely disintermediated by them
Continued upsell/cross-sell into the existing 9,100+ client base, historically the primary driver of ASV growth (more impactful than new logo wins)
Enterprise contract restructuring: average renewed contract terms extended roughly 30% with no price compression, locking in multi-year revenue and improving retention economics
Wealth management vertical expansion — professional user growth in wealth is outpacing the base FactSet user population
Bolt-on M&A expanding adjacent workflow categories: LiquidityBook (trading/OMS, closed Feb 2025, $243.2M) and Irwin (investor relations/capital markets platform, closed Nov 2024, $120.2M)
International/Asia-Pacific expansion, still FactSet's smallest region (~10% of revenue) and a longer-runway growth opportunity

business.risk: AI/LLM disruption of the terminal/workflow model
business.description: Generative AI tools threaten to commoditize basic financial data retrieval and analysis that historically justified premium workstation seat pricing. This is the single largest overhang on the stock and the primary driver of FactSet's ~50%+ decline from 2025 highs; the bear case argues AI could shrink seat counts even if FactSet successfully embeds AI into its own product.

business.risk: Intense competition from larger, better-capitalized rivals
business.description: Bloomberg (~33% share) and LSEG/Refinitiv (~20% share) dominate the market; both have greater scale, data breadth in areas like fixed income/FX, and resources to invest in competing AI capabilities, potentially pressuring FactSet's pricing and win rates.
The ~18% of ASV tied to sell-side/banking clients is more sensitive to capital markets activity, M&A volumes, and bank headcount than the stickier buy-side book.

LiquidityBook and Irwin represent a step-up in acquisition size/frequency versus FactSet's historically organic growth model; successful integration of trading/OMS and IR platforms into the core offering is not guaranteed.

financial.description: Debt/equity around 0.77x and net debt/EBITDA near 1.4x following debt-funded acquisitions (LiquidityBook, Irwin); interest coverage remains healthy (~14x) but leverage has increased from FactSet's historically conservative balance sheet.
With ~35% of revenue generated outside the Americas, USD strength/weakness affects reported (though not organic) ASV and revenue growth.

FY2026 adjusted operating margin guidance of 34.0-35.5% reflects second-half-weighted strategic (AI-related) investment spend, which could compress near-term profitability even as it supports the long-term competitive position.

regulatory.risk: Data privacy and cross-border data regulation
regulatory.description: As a global aggregator of financial and personal data (including in wealth management), FactSet is subject to evolving data privacy regimes (GDPR and similar) across the jurisdictions it operates in.

Emerging AI regulation could affect how FactSet and its partners (Google, Anthropic) can deploy AI agents using licensed/proprietary financial data, particularly around explainability and auditability requirements in regulated finance.

macro.risk: Capital markets and asset management industry sensitivity
macro.description: Demand for FactSet's core client base (asset managers, banks, hedge funds) is correlated with AUM levels, trading volumes, and financial industry headcount, all of which are sensitive to equity market performance and economic cycles.

macro.risk: Cost-cutting pressure on financial industry clients
macro.description: In weak economic conditions, buy-side and sell-side clients scrutinize data/research spend and may consolidate vendors or seek lower-cost alternatives, pressuring ASV growth and seat counts.
Higher rates raise the cost of debt-funded M&A and can pressure asset manager profitability/spending indirectly, though FactSet's own recurring subscription model is not highly rate-sensitive.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The global financial data and analytics market is large (multi-tens of billions of dollars) and growing at a mid-single-digit rate, with AI integration now the dominant strategic theme reshaping competitive dynamics — both a cost/efficiency opportunity for incumbents like FactSet and an existential threat narrative driving investor skepticism in 2026.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate. Subscription-based, high-retention revenue provides resilience, but ASV growth, new client wins, and especially sell-side demand correlate with financial industry health, AUM growth, and capital markets activity.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-moderate direct sensitivity (recurring subscription revenue); moderate indirect sensitivity via financial-industry client budgets and the cost of debt used for acquisitions.
key_input_costs: Technology/cloud infrastructure (AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure)
Skilled labor (engineering, content operations, including offshore centers in India and the Philippines)
AI/LLM compute costs for embedded AI features

recent_developments.event: FactSet scheduled to report Q4 and full fiscal-year 2026 results before market open; consensus estimates ~$628-630M revenue (+5.3-5.5% YoY) and ~$4.35 adjusted EPS versus $4.05 in the prior-year quarter.

Wave of analyst price-target increases ahead of earnings: William Blair upgraded to Outperform; Morgan Stanley raised its target to $300 (Equal-Weight); Deutsche Bank raised to $299 (Hold); RBC raised to $304 (Sector Perform, Aug 27) — signaling improving sentiment after the AI-disruption selloff earlier in 2026.

Q3 FY2026 results: organic ASV grew 7.1% YoY to $2.48B (an acceleration from prior quarters), revenue rose 6.4% YoY to $622.9M, and adjusted EPS grew 6.1% to $4.53. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance and noted it was tracking toward the high end of ranges. ASV retention remained above 95%; average renewed contract terms extended ~30% with no price compression.

Announced a strategic partnership with Google Cloud to embed Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform capabilities into the FactSet Workstation and jointly build AI agents for portfolio operations, deal advisory, and corporate finance workflows.

Shares rose ~6% on news that a new integration lets users bring FactSet market data directly into Anthropic's Claude AI model (via the Cowork enterprise connector), viewed as evidence FactSet's proprietary data could power next-generation AI applications rather than be disintermediated by them.

Stock fell to a 52-week low near $185 (down roughly 50-60% from the 2025 high of ~$387-450) amid an AI-disruption narrative; multiple sell-side downgrades, including Rothschild & Co Redburn (Sell, $215 target) and Barclays (Underweight, target cut to $210), citing fears that AI/LLM tools would erode the value of traditional financial terminal seats.

FactSet reported clients using its AI solutions are growing ASV roughly 50% faster than the rest of the client base, and that over 90% of its top 50 clients by ASV use four or more FactSet AI capabilities — management's core rebuttal to the AI-disruption bear case.

Leadership transition: Sanoke Viswanathan (former JPMorgan executive) became CEO, succeeding long-tenured CEO Phil Snow, who retired after roughly a decade in the role and stayed on as a senior advisor through the end of 2025.

Completed acquisition of LiquidityBook (cloud-native OMS/trading platform with a proprietary FIX network connecting to 200+ brokers and 1,600+ destinations across 80 markets) for $243.2M net of cash acquired.
Completed acquisition of Irwin, an investor relations and capital markets platform for public companies, for $120.2M net of cash acquired.

guidance.management_commentary: On the Q3 FY2026 call, CEO Sanoke Viswanathan emphasized that FactSet's 'four foundational strengths' (data, analytics, workflow integration, and client relationships) are becoming more, not less, valuable as clients deploy AI widely, directly countering the market's AI-disruption thesis. Management highlighted that clients using FactSet's AI solutions grew ASV roughly 50% faster than the rest of the business, and that the majority of ASV renewed in the quarter was structured as enterprise agreements or locked in for three-plus years, with average contract terms extended roughly 30% and no price compression — evidence cited as proof of durable pricing power even amid the AI narrative.

bull_case: AI is proving to be a net positive so far, not a disruptor: clients adopting FactSet's own AI tools are growing ASV ~50% faster than the rest of the book, and over 90% of the top 50 clients use 4+ FactSet AI solutions — early evidence the AI-disruption bear case may be overstated, at least for FactSet's embedded-enterprise model.

Extremely sticky, long-duration client base (95%+ retention, 16+ year average tenure, contracts increasingly multi-year enterprise agreements with no price compression) provides highly visible, recurring cash flows that are difficult for AI-native entrants to displace quickly given regulatory/compliance requirements for sourced, auditable data.

Valuation reset after the 2026 AI-fear selloff (stock fell from ~$387-450 highs to a ~$185 low) may have overcorrected; the recent wave of price-target increases (Morgan Stanley to $300, RBC to $304, Deutsche Bank to $299, William Blair upgrade to Outperform) suggests sell-side sentiment is stabilizing as Q3 FY2026 results beat and ASV growth accelerated to 7.1%.

Partnerships with Google Cloud (Gemini agents) and Anthropic (Claude data connector) position FactSet as critical infrastructure — a trusted, auditable data layer — for AI agents in regulated finance, rather than being disintermediated by them.

Accelerating organic ASV growth (5.5% in FY2025 to 7.1% in Q3 FY2026) alongside reaffirmed high-end guidance tracking, combined with disciplined capital allocation (buybacks, moderate leverage) supports continued EPS growth even with margin investment in AI.
bear_case: The core AI-disruption thesis may still be right, just early: if LLM-based tools eventually commoditize basic data retrieval, screening, and analysis that historically justified premium workstation seat pricing, FactSet's per-seat/per-client economics could erode structurally even as near-term ASV metrics look healthy — the stock's ~50%+ 2026 drawdown shows how quickly this narrative can reprice the shares.

FactSet remains the smaller player against Bloomberg (~33% share) and LSEG/Refinitiv (~20% share), both of which have more resources to invest in competing AI capabilities and greater data breadth, limiting FactSet's ability to win share in a technology arms race.

Margin guidance (34.0-35.5% adjusted operating margin) reflects heavier AI-related investment spend, meaning near-term profitability growth may lag revenue growth as the company spends defensively/offensively to stay ahead of the AI disruption narrative, with no guarantee that spend converts to durable competitive advantage.

Growth remains modest in absolute terms (mid-single-digit-to-high-single-digit organic ASV growth) relative to a rerating that has pushed the stock back toward $300 and consensus price targets in the $290s-$300s — leaving less room for multiple expansion if growth doesn't durably re-accelerate past Q3 FY2026's 7.1% print.

Sell-side/banking-linked ASV (~18% of the book) and broader capital-markets cyclicality expose FactSet to swings in financial industry headcount and spending that are largely outside management's control, and increased leverage from the LiquidityBook/Irwin acquisitions reduces balance sheet flexibility relative to FactSet's historically conservative posture.
